summary: FLAMEWISE is an interactive scientific research dashboard designed to organize and explore NASA-related microgravity combustion investigations. It brings research information, scientific findings, evidence classifications, and references into one accessible platform. By distinguishing verified findings, modeled results, planned experiments, and unverified information, FLAMEWISE helps users explore existing combustion research and better understand its relevance to fire safety in future human space exploration.
details:
FLAMEWISE is an interactive research dashboard created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, under the "Flame in Freefall" challenge. Our goal is to make decades of microgravity combustion research easier to explore, understand, and navigate.

The project brings information from different combustion investigations into one organized platform. Users can browse the research library, search and filter investigations, explore individual study details, review scientific findings, and access the references behind the information.

One of the main features of FLAMEWISE is its focus on scientific evidence and accuracy. Research findings are classified according to their evidence status, helping users distinguish verified information from partial, modeled, planned, derived, or unverified findings. We also keep different investigations and datasets separate, distinguish experimental observations from simulations, and avoid treating missing values as zero. This helps reduce confusion and prevents misleading comparisons.

We developed FLAMEWISE as a web-based dashboard using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. We used Visual Studio Code for development and GitHub for source-code management and public hosting through GitHub Pages.

What makes our project creative is the way it turns scattered and complex scientific research into an accessible, structured, and interactive experience. Instead of presenting research as disconnected documents, FLAMEWISE gives users a clearer way to navigate investigations and understand how different findings relate to the broader field of space fire safety.

During development, our team considered scientific reliability, clarity, accessibility, usability, and the importance of showing the limitations of available evidence. We wanted the platform to be informative without making unsupported scientific claims.

Our intended impact is to help students, researchers, and space enthusiasts explore existing combustion research more efficiently and better understand the scientific knowledge relevant to fire safety in future human missions to the Moon and Mars.

FLAMEWISE is a research exploration and organization tool designed to support informed understanding, not a certified fire-safety prediction system.
